import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 as per hint 21
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_13/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_13/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (shared column)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on='city')

# Group by 'type' (primary key in target)
# Aggregate sum of driver_count from source0 and count of ride_id from source1
agg = joined.groupby('type').agg({
    'driver_count': 'sum',
    'ride_id': 'count'
}).reset_index()

# According to target schema, only 'type' and 'driver_count' are needed
# The target driver_count = 1187 matches count of rides for Urban type in source1
# So we use the count of rides (ride_id) as driver_count in target
# But the FD says type -> driver_count, so driver_count must come from aggregation on source1 rides count

# Rename 'ride_id' count to 'driver_count' to match target schema
agg = agg.rename(columns={'ride_id': 'driver_count'})

# Select only columns in target schema
result = agg[['type', 'driver_count']]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_13/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
